vulnerable_statements.reason: bfq_split_bfqq(bic, bfqq) drops the bic's process reference to old_bfqq (bfq_put_queue/bfq_release_process_ref). If that was the last reference, old_bfqq is freed. Reading old_bfqq->waker_bfqq afterwards is a use-after-free. The stale waker pointer is then linked into a woken_list via hlist_add_head, which can corrupt memory.
This call may release the last reference to old_bfqq. The function still keeps old_bfqq and dereferences it afterwards.

suggested_fix: Read old_bfqq->waker_bfqq into a local variable before calling bfq_split_bfqq(), while the reference to bfqq is still held. Then use that saved value (or re-validate it) after the split, and do not touch old_bfqq after the split. Another option is to take an extra reference on old_bfqq around the split and drop it after copying the waker. The upstream fix saves the waker before splitting and stops dereferencing old_bfqq after bfq_split_bfqq().
